text:
Let [t] denote the greatest integer less than or equal to t. Let 
f(x) = x $-$ [x], g(x) = 1 $-$ x + [x], and h(x) = min{f(x), g(x)}, x $\in$ [$-$2, 2]. Then h is :
options:
continuous in [$-$2, 2] but not differentiable at more than 
four points in ($-$2, 2)
not continuous at exactly three points in [$-$2, 2]

continuous in [$-$2, 2] but not differentiable at exactly 
three points in ($-$2, 2)
not continuous at exactly four points in [$-$2, 2]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With $\{x\}=x-[x]\in [0,1)$, $f(x)=\{x\}$ and $g(x)=1-\{x\}$, so

$h(x)=\min (\{x\},1-\{x\})=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \{x\}, & 0\leq \{x\}\leq \dfrac{1}{2} \\ 1-\{x\}, & \dfrac{1}{2}<\{x\}<1 \end{array} \right.$

On each interval $[n,n+1]$, $h$ rises with slope 1 from 0 at $x=n$ to $\dfrac{1}{2}$ at $x=n+\dfrac{1}{2}$, then falls with slope $-1$ to 0 at $x=n+1$.


[IMG]

Inside each $(n,n+1)$, $h$ is continuous. At an integer $n$, $h(n)=\min (0,1)=0$; as $x\to n^{+}$, $\{x\}\to 0$ so $h\to 0$, and as $x\to n^{-}$, $1-\{x\}\to 0$ so $h\to 0$. Hence $h$ is continuous on $[-2,2]$, which rules out (B) and (D).

The slope changes from $-1$ to $1$ at every integer and from $1$ to $-1$ at every half-integer. In $(-2,2)$ these are $-1,0,1$ and $-\dfrac{3}{2},-\dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{3}{2}$, so $h$ is not differentiable at 7 points, more than four.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
Let y(x) be the solution of the differential equation 

$2x^{2} dy + (e^{y}$ $-$ 2x)dx = 0, x > 0. If y(e) = 1, then y(1) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$2x^{2}dy+(e^{y}-2x)dx=0$

$\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{e^{y}-2x}{2x^{2}}=0\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{e^{y}}{2x^{2}}-\frac{1}{x}=0$

$e^{-y}\frac{dy}{dx}-\frac{e^{-y}}{x}=-\frac{1}{2x^{2}}\Rightarrow$ Put $e^{-y}=z$

$\frac{-dz}{dx}-\frac{z}{x}=-\frac{1}{2x^{2}}\Rightarrow xdz+zdx=\frac{dx}{2x}$

$d(xz)=\frac{dx}{2x}\Rightarrow xz=\frac{1}{2}\log _{e}x+c$

$xe^{-y}=\frac{1}{2}\log _{e}x+c$, passes through (e, 1)

$\Rightarrow C=\frac{1}{2}$

$xe^{-y}=\frac{\log _{e}ex}{2}$

$e^{-y}=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow y=\log _{e}2$

text: The locus of the mid points of the chords of the hyperbola $x^{2}$ $-$ $y^{2} = 4$, which touch the parabola $y^{2} = 8x$, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $(h,k)$ be the midpoint of a chord of $x^{2}-y^{2}=4$. By $T=S_{1}$, the chord is $hx-ky=h^{2}-k^{2}$, i.e.

$y=\frac{h}{k}x-\frac{h^{2}-k^{2}}{k}$

The line $y=mx+c$ touches $y^{2}=8x$ (here $a=2$) when $c=\dfrac{2}{m}$.

With $m=\dfrac{h}{k}$ and $c=\dfrac{k^{2}-h^{2}}{k}$:

$\frac{k^{2}-h^{2}}{k}=\frac{2k}{h}\Rightarrow h(k^{2}-h^{2})=2k^{2}\Rightarrow k^{2}(h-2)=h^{3}$

So the locus is $y^{2}(x-2)=x^{3}$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Evening Shift

text: Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, ......., a_{10}$ be an AP with common difference $-$ 3 and $b_{1}, b_{2}, ........., b_{10}$ be a GP with common ratio 2. Let $c_{k} = a_{k} + b_{k}, k = 1, 2, ......, 10$. If $c_{2} = 12$ and $c_{3} = 13$, then $\sum\limits _{k=1}^{10}c_{k}$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$a_{1},a_{2},a_{3},\ldots ,a_{10}$ are in AP common difference $=-3$

 $b_{1},b_{2},b_{3},\ldots ,b_{10}$ are in GP common ratio $=2$

 Since, $c_{k}=a_{k}+b_{k},k=1,2,3\ldots \ldots ,10$

$\therefore c_{2}=a_{2}+b_{2}=12$

$c_{3}=a_{3}+b_{3}=13$

Now, $\mathrm{C}_{3}-\mathrm{C}_{2}=1$

$\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow  & (a_{3}-a_{2})+(b_{3}-b_{2})\neq 1\Rightarrow -3+(2b_{2}-b_{2})\neq 1 \\ \Rightarrow  & b_{2}=4 \\ \therefore  & a_{2}=8 \end{array}$

So, AP is $11,8,5,\ldots$.

Now, $\sum\limits _{k=1}^{10}C_{k}=\sum\limits _{k=1}^{10}a_{k}+\sum\limits _{k=1}^{10}b_{k}$

$\begin{array}{l} =\left (\dfrac{10}{2}\right )[22+9(-3)]+2\left (\dfrac{2^{10}-1}{2-1}\right ) \\ =5(22-27)+2(1023)=2046-25 \\ =2021 \end{array}$
